In summary, our research is concerned with
the response of the climate to a change in Earth’s obliquities.
climate feedbacks and climate change, and in particular, the role of the ocean in the response to changes in Earth’s obliquitiy.
understanding the role of the atmosphere and ocean on the evolution of the Earth’s climate and its response to orbital forcing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the feedbacks involved in response to a change in obliquity are complex and involve a number of processes, including changes in the atmospheric and oceanic circulation, the surface albedo, and the water vapor content.
a reduction in obliquitiy increases the global mean temperature by about 1 K, but the global mean surface temperature decreases by about 1/2 of a degree.
climate feedbacks in response to changes in obliquity can be quite strong, and the sign of the feedback is not determined by the sign of the forcing alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we investigated how the climate system responds to a change in the Earth’s obliquities.
the feedbacks in the climate system are strong enough to counteract the change in the direct insolation, leading to a global mean temperature decrease despite that the change is close to zero.
the Earth’s climate system has the potential to amplify or damp the effect of changes in the obliquity, depending on the location.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the response of climate is complex and depends on many processes.
the climate response to changes in obliquity is not a simple one-to-one relation with the change in insolation.
a change in the obliquity has a significant influence on the climate system.
